Nigerius, also known as the River King, is the revered deity of the Niger River, one of the longest rivers in Africa that flows through West Africa. Nigerius is a powerful and majestic god, associated with the mighty waters of the Niger River and regarded as a divine ruler of the river's realm.

Nigerius is often depicted as a regal figure with a crown or headdress adorned with river-related symbols, such as fish, crocodiles, and water plants. He is often shown with a trident or a staff, representing his dominion over the river's currents, floods, and tributaries. Nigerius is also associated with fertility and abundance, as the Niger River is a lifeline for the people living in the region, providing water for irrigation, transportation, and livelihoods.

As the River King, Nigerius is believed to have control over the Niger River and its tributaries, regulating the flow of water and ensuring the well-being of the surrounding lands and people. He is also regarded as a protector of the river's ecosystems and wildlife, promoting responsible use of its resources and conservation of its natural beauty.

Nigerius is honored with various rituals, ceremonies, and festivities by the people living along the Niger River. Offerings of food, livestock, and other items are made to Nigerius as a sign of reverence and gratitude. His name is invoked in prayers, songs, and rituals, seeking his blessings for favorable weather, smooth navigation, and abundant harvests. Nigerius is celebrated as a symbol of power, fertility, and protection, and his worship is an integral part of the culture and traditions of the Niger River basin.
